title: Introduce read-slicing proxy and prune legacy fetchers to reduce console tail latency
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Background: The console backend still routes many front-end queries through a set of legacy fetcher modules that were incrementally stitched on top of the original aggregator. These legacy fetchers introduce extra fanout, duplicate reads, and inconsistent cache keys which amplify 95/99th percentile latency during spikes. Goal: Introduce a lightweight read-slicing proxy layer that centralizes request coalescing, enforces canonical cache keys, and optionally prefetches hot related data. Concurrently, prune and decommission obsolete fetcher paths (legacy user list fetcher and old metrics rollup endpoint) to reduce code surface and memory churn. This ticket covers design, incremental implementation, integration tests, and an observability-driven roll-out with automatic rollback on regression.
scope:
- Implement read-slicing proxy service as a sidecar within the console aggregator pod.
- Add adaptive coalescing per-request-key with a short window (5-15ms).
- Normalize cache key generation across GraphQL and REST bridges.
- Introduce optional prefetch for top-N related entities (configurable).
- Decommission legacy fetchers: userlist_v1_fetcher and metrics_rollup_legacy.
- Add end-to-end tests and bench harness.
Non-goals: full rewrite of aggregator state machine, Mobile SDKs or external API clients changes.
tasks: Design read-slicing proxy API and config (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Read-Slicing+Proxy+Design)
Prototype in-memory coalescer (bench locally with synthetic traffic)
Implement proxy as express + worker-pool sidecar in console-aggregator image
Canonicalize cache key utility used by graphql resolver and rest bridge
Create migration shim to route 25% traffic through proxy for A/B test
Write integration tests (playback and stubbing of downstream services)
Create PRs and get cross-team reviews (runtime, infra, observability)
Decommission legacy fetchers behind feature flag and run 24h soak
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end 95p and 99p tail latency for console list endpoints reduced by >= 20% in A/B experiment
Cache key mismatch rate < 0.1% across sampled traffic
No increased error rate (>1% delta) or dropped requests during 25% traffic rollout
All legacy fetcher code paths gated with feature flag removed and corresponding tests deleted
Perf bench shows reduced CPU allocation for aggregator under same QPS (>=10% lower median CPU)
Runbook updated with rollback steps and observability dashboards
risks: Proxy coalescing window may add latency for low-cardinality, single-request patterns
Canonicalizing cache keys incorrectly could surface stale reads or cache poisoning
Decommissioning legacy endpoints could break internal tooling that depends on their response shapes
Increased complexity in deployment (sidecar) may require infra coordination for resource limits
mitigations: Start with a small coalescing window (5ms) and profile impact; make window configurable per-route
Add strict integration tests and sampled tracing to compare responses between old and new paths
Coordinate with Platform and Customer Success to identify internal consumers before removal
Deploy sidecar behind feature flag and require infra review for pod resource requests/limits
observability: Dashboards: Console Aggregator -> Read-Slicing Proxy overview (QPS, coalesced %, tail latency)
Traces: sample 1% of coalesced requests with full span to downstream services
Benchmarks: run nightly bench job comparing baseline sha and candidate sha and store results
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonical cache key generation and key migration shim
Integration tests with in-memory downstream mocks to verify semantic parity
Load tests at 2x peak QPS with varying payload sizes (execute in perf env)
Canary rollout: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 75% with automated monitoring gates
Rollback policy: auto rollback on error rate delta > 0.5% or 99p latency regression > 15%
rollout_plan: Deploy to staging and run full integration suite
Canary to us-east only at 5% for 2 hours; analyze dashboards
Ramp to 25% for 24 hours; run long-tail bench and soak tests
Full rollout after 72h of stable metrics
Flip feature flag off to rollback; remove legacy code in a follow-up cleanup cycle
notes: Initial prototype reduced duplicated downstream calls by ~35% in local bench
Observed one legacy consumer relying on metrics_rollup_legacy; contact @Evan Torres to schedule migration
Corresponding infra ticket required to add sidecar resource limits: INF-1987
Suggested follow-up: integrate prefetch heuristics with Optimize's workload profiler
